title: Countable, uncountable and quantifiers
titleVi: Danh từ đếm được, không đếm được và lượng từ
summary: Danh sách danh từ không đếm được người Việt hay chia số nhiều, cùng much/many, few/little và các đơn vị đo.
whyItMatters: *Informations, advices, furnitures* là những lỗi mà người Việt mắc nhiều nhất vì tiếng Việt cho phép nói *những thông tin*, *những lời khuyên*. Trong Writing Task 1 và 2, nhóm từ này xuất hiện ở mọi đoạn — *information, research, evidence, data* — nên chỉ một lỗi chia số nhiều cũng đủ làm giám khảo ghi nhận là lỗi hệ thống.

sections.heading: The basic split
body: **Countable** nouns have singular and plural forms and can be counted: *a book, two books, three questions.* **Uncountable** nouns have no plural and take a singular verb: *information, water, research.*

*a/an* only works with singular countable nouns. Plural countable nouns can stand alone (*Books are expensive*) and uncountable nouns can stand alone (*Water is essential*). This is why *a water* is wrong but *some water* is fine.

Some nouns are countable in one meaning and uncountable in another. *Chicken* (the animal) is countable; *chicken* (the meat) is uncountable. *Paper* (material) is uncountable; *a paper* (a newspaper or an essay) is countable.

sections.heading: The list Vietnamese speakers must memorise
body: These nouns are uncountable in English even though their Vietnamese equivalents are countable or can take *những*: **advice, information, news, evidence, research, knowledge, progress, work, homework, housework, furniture, equipment, machinery, luggage, baggage, accommodation, software, transport, traffic, scenery, weather, behaviour, permission, vocabulary, money**.
None of them takes *-s*, and all take a singular verb: *The news is good*, *This equipment is expensive*, *Her research focuses on...*, *The traffic was heavy.*
A few of them look plural but are singular: *news*, *mathematics*, *physics*, *economics*, *politics* (as a subject). *The news is on at nine.*

examples.right: She gave me some useful advice.
examples.wrong: She gave me some useful advices.
examples.note: *advice* không có số nhiều; muốn đếm thì dùng *a piece of advice*.

examples.right: The research was conducted over two years.
examples.wrong: The researches were conducted over two years.
examples.note: *research* không đếm được; nhiều nghiên cứu thì nói *several studies*.
Động từ chia **số ít** với danh từ không đếm được.

sections.heading: much, many, a lot of, little, few
body: **many** and **few** go with plural countable nouns; **much** and **little** go with uncountables. **a lot of / lots of** works with both and is the natural choice in positive sentences: *a lot of students*, *a lot of traffic*.
**much** is unusual in positive statements. *I have much work* sounds formal or unnatural; say *I have a lot of work.* Keep *much* for negatives and questions: *There isn't much time.*

**a few** and **a little** mean "some, a small amount" and are positive. **few** and **little** without *a* mean "almost none" and are negative: *Few people attended* (almost nobody came) versus *A few people attended* (some came).

rows: There isn't much demand for it.
A lot of research has been done.
A few students failed. / Few students failed.
There is a little time left. / There is little time left.

sections.heading: some, any and no
body: **some** in positive statements, **any** in negatives and questions: *We collected some data. We didn't collect any data. Did you collect any data?*
**some** also appears in questions when you expect a yes, or when offering: *Would you like some coffee? Could you give me some feedback?* This is polite, not a grammar error.
**no + noun** makes the verb positive: *There are no vacancies* (= *There aren't any vacancies*). Do not double the negative: *There aren't no vacancies* is non-standard.

examples.right: There wasn't any evidence to support the claim.

examples.wrong: There wasn't no additional funding provided.
examples.note: **no** thay cho *not any*, không dùng cả hai.

sections.heading: Counting the uncountable: partitives
body: To count an uncountable noun, use a **partitive**: a unit word plus *of*. *A piece of advice, a piece of information, an item of furniture, a sheet of paper, a slice of bread, a bar of chocolate, a bottle of water, a grain of rice, a litre of petrol.*
The plural goes on the partitive, not on the noun: *two pieces of advice*, *three items of equipment*, *several sheets of paper*. This is the structure that fixes the *advices* error permanently.

Some dual-meaning nouns shift with the partitive: *a hair* (one strand) versus *hair* (the mass); *an experience* (one event) versus *experience* (knowledge); *a noise* (one sound) versus *noise* (the phenomenon); *a room* (one room) versus *room* (space).

rows: a piece of advice / two pieces of advice
a piece of information / an item of information
a piece of furniture / an item of furniture
a slice of bread / a loaf of bread
a study / a piece of research

commonMistakes.wrong: My teacher gave me some good advices.
commonMistakes.right: My teacher gave me some good advice.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt nói *những lời khuyên* nên người học thêm *-s*. **advice** là danh từ không đếm được; muốn đếm phải dùng **a piece of advice**.

commonMistakes.wrong: I have a good news for you.
commonMistakes.right: I have some good news for you.
commonMistakes.why: **news** không đếm được và luôn chia **số ít**: *The news is good.* Không dùng *a news* hay *newses*.

commonMistakes.right: The report contains a lot of information.
commonMistakes.why: **information** không có số nhiều, và *many* chỉ đi với danh từ đếm được số nhiều. Dùng **much/a lot of** hoặc đổi sang *many facts*.

commonMistakes.wrong: The furnitures in the flat are old.
commonMistakes.right: The furniture in the flat is old.
commonMistakes.why: **furniture** không đếm được nên không có *-s* và động từ chia số ít. Đây là lỗi hệ thống, lặp lại ở mọi đoạn văn tả nội thất.

commonMistakes.wrong: There are less students in this class than last year.
commonMistakes.right: There are fewer students in this class than last year.
commonMistakes.why: **less** dùng cho không đếm được, **fewer** cho số nhiều đếm được. *Students* đếm được nên phải là *fewer*.

ieltsTips: Trong Task 1, dùng `the amount of + không đếm được` và `the number of + đếm được số nhiều` — cặp này xuất hiện ở gần như mọi bài mô tả biểu đồ.
Viết `a significant amount of research` chứ không phải `many researches`; đổi sang `several studies` nếu cần số nhiều.
Khi mô tả xu hướng, `fewer people` và `less traffic` là cặp chính xác — dùng sai sẽ bị coi là lỗi ngữ pháp cơ bản.
Học danh từ không đếm được theo cụm đo: `a piece of advice`, `an item of equipment`, `a sheet of paper` — vừa đúng ngữ pháp vừa tăng điểm từ vựng.

exercises.question: The researcher collected ___ information over six months.
exercises.explanation: *information* không đếm được → **a great deal of**; *many* và *a large number of* chỉ dùng với số nhiều đếm được.

exercises.question: There are ___ applicants this year than last year.
Could you give me ___ information about the course?
Which sentence is correct?
exercises.explanation: *equipment* không đếm được → không có *-s*, động từ số ít, không dùng *an*.

exercises.question: ___ people attended the meeting, so it was cancelled.
exercises.explanation: **Few** (không có *a*) nghĩa là *rất ít, gần như không có* — phù hợp với việc phải hủy buổi họp.

exercises.question: She gave me two ___ of advice before the interview.
exercises.explanation: **a piece of advice** → số nhiều *two pieces of advice*.

exercises.question: The news ___ (be) better than we expected.
exercises.explanation: **news** chia số ít: *The news is/was better...*

exercises.question: We don't have ___ time left before the deadline.
exercises.explanation: *time* không đếm được, câu phủ định → **much** hoặc **any**.

exercises.question: There is ___ hope of finding a cheap flat in the centre.
The government has invested a great ___ in public transport.
exercises.explanation: **a great deal of** + danh từ không đếm được.
